claims_about_writeup.quote: `contribution.md` (296 words) credits WBS for the direction and claims the prefix-anchor finding, the dose/band protocol, and the contrast survey as this submission's contribution.
claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up is approximately 295-296 words, explicitly names 'white-bear steering, Raman et al. 2026' and states it 'adds this same contrast through the prompt and recommends the read cell as the cheapest anchor' (crediting WBS for the direction), while framing 'The new contribution is where the direction is anchored' and detailing the dose window, band 20-24, and the six-contrast search (contrast survey) as the submission's own contribution.

message_source_quote: `papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md` turned out to be direct prior art for exactly this task (think/don't-think direction, band 20–24, 0.14→0.83 on their split) — a straight reproduction would score ~0 on novelty, so I needed a distinguishable method.
writeup_source_quote:
The prior stance-steering study
(white-bear steering, Raman et al. 2026) adds this same contrast through the prompt and recommends the read cell
as the cheapest anchor.

differences.message_quote: papers/raman2026-white-bear-steering.md` turned out to be direct prior art for exactly this task (think/don't-think direction, band 20–24, 0.14→0.83 on their split) — a straight reproduction would score ~0 on novelty
differences.writeup_quote: The prior stance-steering study (white-bear steering, Raman et al. 2026) adds this same contrast through the prompt and recommends the read cell as the cheapest anchor.
differences.what: The message explicitly states that WBS itself achieves a 0.14→0.83 result on its own split using the same band/direction, and bluntly says a straight reproduction of WBS would score ~0 on novelty, underscoring how close the underlying method is to WBS. The write-up only describes WBS qualitatively (that it adds the same contrast via the prompt and recommends the read cell) without stating WBS's own reported result or the near-reproduction framing.

differences.message_quote: an early misreading of WBS's k-units (k=6 ≈ 4.2 units/layer, not 6) nearly sent me off the peak.
differences.what: The message reveals that the author was working directly from WBS's own dosing/unit scheme (and initially misapplied it), showing a tighter operational dependence on WBS's specifics than the write-up discloses; the write-up gives its own dose numbers with no mention of deriving or misreading them from WBS.

rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. 2026 / white-bear steering (WBS) as the prior work whose think/don't-think contrast construction the method reuses, and both frame the sole novelty as relocating the injection site to the prefix tokens (reporting the same prefix > read-cell > content-position ordering). The message, however, goes further than the write-up in spelling out how close the method otherwise is to WBS — citing WBS's own reported result and an episode of directly following (and misreading) WBS's dosing units — details the write-up omits while still crediting WBS for the direction and the prompt-based approach.
